conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I’ll be your doctor during this stay. You came in with abdominal pain, nausea, and some diarrhea. Can you tell me more about what’s been going on?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, thank you. I’ve had this dull, constant pain in my upper belly for about a day. It’s different from my usual G-tube site pain. Feels more like the ulcers I’ve had before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That makes sense. Given your history of gastric bypass and previous marginal ulcers, we need to check if it’s ulcer-related again. We’ve done some blood work and an X-ray.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. My lipase was high last time—was it high again?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, your lipase was elevated—186, which is about three times the upper limit. That raised concern for pancreatitis, but your symptoms and history make us also think about ulcers or bowel overgrowth.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve had dumping syndrome and bacterial overgrowth before. Could that be flaring up?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Absolutely. That’s part of our differential. The X-ray showed no free air or obstruction, which is good. But your bladder was very full—possibly contributing to discomfort.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I haven’t felt the urge to go. Should I be worried?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll monitor it. No need for a catheter unless it persists. For now, we’re starting IV fluids and holding your tube feeds temporarily—bowel rest—to see if your pancreas settles down.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. And my pain? It’s still pretty constant.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We gave you dilaudid in the ER, and we’ll continue with pain meds as needed. We’re also starting a proton-pump inhibitor to protect your stomach lining, just in case it’s an ulcer.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi again. Your labs are stable, and your lipase has already dropped to 118. That’s a good sign. We’re still concerned about the cause, so we’ve scheduled an MRCP tomorrow to look at your pancreas and bile ducts.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that an MRI? I’ve had those before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it’s a special MRI that focuses on the pancreas and bile system. It will help us rule out gallstones or inflammation. We’ll also give you some oral contrast through your G-tube to check for dumping syndrome.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will it show if I have another ulcer?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: MRCP isn’t the best for ulcers. If we’re still suspicious, we may do an EGD—a scope down through your stomach—to look directly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your MRCP results are back. Good news—your pancreas and bile ducts look completely normal. No signs of inflammation or blockage.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So it’s not pancreatitis?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Unlikely. The elevated lipase might be from your medications—fluoxetine has a small risk. But your symptoms still point to possible ulcer. We’re scheduling an EGD this afternoon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve had a few of those. Will they treat anything they find?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. If there’s an ulcer, they can cauterize it if it’s bleeding or has a lesion. We’ll also restart your tube feeds after, using a low-protein formula to avoid stressing your system.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I remember last time—high protein made me confused. Is that still a concern?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. Your prior workup suggested a possible urea cycle issue. We’re still waiting on genetic results, but we’ll keep protein low for now to be safe.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi. Your EGD is done. You had a marginal ulcer near the gastric bypass site, and there was a small pigmented lesion. It’s been cauterized, so it should heal.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is it cancerous?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No biopsy was taken, but the appearance wasn’t concerning. Still, we’ll repeat the EGD in 8 weeks to make sure it’s healing.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that’s a relief. What about my meds?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re increasing your pantoprazole to twice daily and adding sucralfate four times a day. That helps protect the ulcer site. You’ll take the sucralfate by mouth, not through the tube.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Why by mouth?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Because it coats the upper stomach and esophagus better when swallowed. It helps form a protective layer over the ulcer.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. Can I restart my tube feeds now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’re restarting them now—low protein NutriHep, continuous drip. We’ll monitor for nausea or pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: How are you feeling? Any pain or nausea since restarting feeds?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Much better. Pain is down to a 3. Still a little bloated, but no vomiting.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. Your labs today also look better—lipase is normal, and your kidney function is good. We’re planning to discharge you tomorrow if this continues.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will I need pain meds at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll give you a short course of oxycodone for breakthrough pain. But we’ll also start a bowel regimen—senna and docusate—since narcotics can cause constipation.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve had that before. I’ll take them as needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Also, your fluoxetine and atenolol are continuing. No changes there. And we’ll keep rifaximin for bacterial overgrowth prevention.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What about H. pylori? Should I be tested?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: GI wants a stool antigen test, but you haven’t had a bowel movement this admission. Please follow up with them in clinic to get it done.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. You’ve done really well overnight—no pain, tolerating feeds, vitals stable. We’re clearing you for discharge.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. What do I need to do at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Continue pantoprazole twice daily and sucralfate four times a day by mouth. Keep using NutriHep with low protein. Take oxycodone only if needed for pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the bowel meds?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, senna and docusate twice daily while on oxycodone. They’ll help prevent constipation.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: When do I see GI again?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: In 8 weeks for a repeat EGD. They’ll check how the ulcer is healing. Call sooner if you have severe pain, vomiting, or black stools.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you for explaining everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. You’ve made great progress. We’ll send all instructions to your husband. Take care, and we’ll see you in follow-up.
